Where a Nonlinear Term's Coefficients Begin

Source: R/nonlinear.R
term_coef_start.NlTerm.Rd

Returns the coefficients at which term_build() built the block: the starting value of each of the term's own parameters carried through its link, from start where the caller gave one, and coefficient zero for a parameter that start does not name. The block is the Jacobian at those values, so it is a different block at any other point. Where target is given (the response on the scale of the predictor, which the fitting layer supplies), the parameters that start does not fix are estimated from it by least squares. Zero coefficients are a poor start for a nonlinear term, since the block is then linearized at a point where the function was not meant to be evaluated, and every quantity read at those coefficients, such as the top of the path of a kinked penalty, depends on that point.

The search is a deterministic grid on each free parameter's own chart, polished from the best grid points by stats::optimize() for one parameter and by Nelder-Mead for several, so that a start does not depend on the random seed. The parameters in which the function is jointly affine are solved by least squares at each point of the grid instead of being searched over. They are found with stats::D() by removing repeatedly from the set of parameters every one whose derivative names a member of the set (including the parameter itself); for a function given as an opaque fn the set is empty. Where a parameter is developed over a break-point term, each break-point is then started as described in nl().

The box that each grid spans comes from the data: the quantiles, the standard deviation and the range of the response and of every covariate that the formula names, carried through the parameter's own link and widened, because a parameter may be measured in the units of the response or of a covariate and the box has to cover both.

It is a starting value and is allowed to be approximate; anything that fails leaves the coefficients that term_build() computed.

Arguments

term

A built NlTerm().

target

Optional numeric vector, one per observation: the response on the scale of the predictor. If it is absent, the coefficients are those that term_build() computed.

...

Unused.

Value

A numeric vector, one value per column of the block.
